subject: Human Evolution
title: Laetoli's Frozen Walk
description: A quick, practical guide to Laetoli's Frozen Walk.

hook.text: 3.6 million years ago, two hominins walked through fresh volcanic ash in Tanzania—and left proof.

buildup.text: Rain hardened the ash like cement, preserving 27 metres of footprints before more ash buried them.

discovery.text: The prints show a heel strike, arch, and big-toe push-off—a fully modern bipedal gait.

twist.text: No tools exist from this period. These hominins walked like us but had brains the size of a chimp's.

climax.text: Laetoli proves walking was the first major human adaptation—millions of years before intelligence.

punchline.text: Feet led the way. Brains followed later.

quiz.question: What do the Laetoli footprints demonstrate?
options: Modern bipedal gait existed 3.6 million years ago
